newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Citra Tubindo sees 1997 profits up 71 pct.
newsitem.headline: Citra Tubindo sees 1997 profits up 71 pct.

text.p: PT Citra Tubindo, the Indonesian steel firm supplying oil and gas pipeline products, said on Monday it was targeting profit growth of 71 percent to 26.9 billion rupiah in 1997.
Kris Wiluan, president director, made the prediction in a speech to mark a strategic alliance between Citra Tubindo and Japan's Nippon Steel Corp (NSC).

"With the increase in oil and gas activities around the region, especially the development of the Natuna project, we are very optimistic of the continuing growth of Citra Tubindo and in the success of our partnership with NSC," Wiluan said.
Wiluan was speaking at a tree-planting ceremony at Citra Tubindo's factory on the Indonesian island of Batam.
His 1997 forecast followed an upbeat view of 1996 profits, which he said would be 15.5 billion rupiah, 11 times up on 1995 and almost double the group's original forecast of 8.5 billion rupiah.
He saw earnings per share improving to 600 rupiah in 1997 from 349 rupiah in 1996 and 28 rupiah in 1995.
Wiluan said the tie-up with NSC, operator of the world's largest steel mill, would help Citra Tubindo increase exports to a planned 50 percent of production. -- Singapore (65 8703011)
